{{Quote|Selligores are aquatic mammals native to the temperate and tropical waters of the planet Corsin, a planet once famed for its swoop races but now notorious for a rather brutal Imperial crackdown ''[…]''|Holobrochure for the Tagge Holographic Museum of Chandrila|<ref name="Creatures" />}}
'''Corsin''' was a beautiful [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Greater Plooriod sector/Legends|Greater Plooriod sector]]. Situated at the junction of the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] and [[Vaathkree Trade Corridor/Legends|Vaathkree Trade Corridor]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperspace routes]], it had a [[Temperature/Legends|warm]] climate in its tropical regions and was [[Homeworld/Legends|home]] to the large [[Water/Legends|aquatic]] [[Mammal/Legends|mammal]] [[selligore]]. The creatures [[Diet/Legends|fed]] on [[Plant/Legends|plants]] as well as small [[Fish/Legends|fish]] and [[Plankton/Legends|plankton]], and the [[Tinn'lyi]] nation, native to the planet's [[Tinn'lyi Islands]], maintained a symbiotic relationship with them where the selligores were given gathered plants to eat in exchange for helping catch fish in large nets they dragged behind them.

Originally a subject world of the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]], Corsin was [[Raid on Corsin|raided]] by the [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]] during the conflict known as the [[Mandalorian Wars]]. Approximately three [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] later, the renowned [[Biologist/Legends|bioanalyst]] [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Ronda]] was [[Death/Legends|perished]] on Corsin when the [[Ronda's shuttle|shuttle]] he was on crash-landed. The [[Human/Legends|Human]] future [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Nalia Adollu]] was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] on the planet more than two [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] later. By [[1004 BBY]], Corsin had become a part of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], and during the [[Light and Darkness War|final phase]] of the [[New Sith Wars]] around that time, the Republic's [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] was victorious over the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] in an [[Battle of Corsin|engagement]] at that world. [[Officer/Legends|Officers]] of the Republic's [[Planetary Security Forces]] met at the Corsin venue known as the [[Corsin Retreat]] after the [[Mandalorian Excision]] of [[738 BBY]] to discuss best practices for coordinating action.

By the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Corsin had become a liberal and free-thinking world that also hosted one of the most popular [[Swoop racing/Legends|swoop races]] in the [[Greater Plooriod Cluster]]. While the
[[Journalist/Legends|reporter]] [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]] was covering one such event, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] carried out a brutal [[Crackdown on Corsin|subjugation]] of Corsin, with [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] arresting Na'al and other journalists. While Na'al was spending three [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] in detention, [[Corsin planetary government|Corsin's planetary government]] was replaced with a pro-Imperial regime.

The directives of Corsin's new government led to the infringement upon the natural habitats of the selligores. During the later fragmentation of the Empire, the planet fell within the [[Zsinj's Empire|territory]] controlled by Imperial [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Zsinj]], with the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] suffering a [[Battle of Corsin (5 ABY)|defeat]] there in [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]]. By [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], however, Corsin had been integrated into the New Republic's holdings, and a century later, the planet was a part of [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]].

==Description==
{{Quote|Selligores have long fed and lived along the coasts of their world, primarily surviving in shallow waters (less than 100 meters deep), with regular forays to the surface.|Holobrochure for the Tagge Holographic Museum of Chandrila|<ref name="Creatures" />}}
[[File:CorsinRoutes-TEA.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Corsin was located in the Expansion Region, at the junction of the Hydian Way and the Vaathkree Trade Corridor.]]
Corsin was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Creatures" /> located in the [[Corsin system/Legends|Corsin system]], a part of the [[Greater Plooriod sector/Legends|Greater Plooriod sector]]<ref name="EGTW" /> in the [[Northern Dependencies/Legends|Northern Dependencies]] portion of<ref name="TEA" /> the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]].<ref name="EGTW" /> It was also located in the [[Greater Plooriod Cluster]].<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|362|Greater Plooriod Cluster}}</ref>

By approximately [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], Corsin was situated at the endpoint of the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperspace routes]] known as the [[Corsin Run]] and the [[Mandalorian Road]], which linked it to the [[Bogden system/Legends|Bogden]] and [[Ploo system/Legends|Ploo systems]], respectively. At some point following approximately [[3693 BBY]], those routes became integrated into the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]-spanning [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroute]],<ref name="TEA" /> which connected Corsin to the [[Leafar system/Legends|Leafar system]]<ref name="EGTW" /> as well as the [[Skorrupon system/Legends|Skorrupon system]] of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim's]] [[Trans-Vulta sector/Legends|Trans-Vulta sector]].<ref name="Mid Rim">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-extra-sectors-of-the-mid-rim|text=Essential Atlas Extra: Sectors of the Mid Rim}}</ref> In addition, the hyperlane known as the [[Vaathkree Trade Corridor/Legends|Vaathkree Trade Corridor]] linked it to the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim's]] [[Comkin system/Legends|Comkin system]],<ref name="TEA" /> while another [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] route connected Corsin to<ref name="EGTW" /> the [[Ploo sector/Legends|Ploo sector]].<ref name="Expansion">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-extra-expansion-region|text=Essential Atlas Extra: Expansion Region}}</ref> Corsin's [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] was such that forty-five [[local year]]s were approximately equivalent to forty-two [[Standard year/Legends|years]].<ref name="Creatures" /> A light-[[Color/Legends|colored]] celestial body loomed large in the planet's [[Atmosphere/Legends|sky]].<ref name="EGTW" />

[[File:Selligore.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Corsin was home to the aquatic mammals known as selligores.]]
Corsin was a beautiful world, the surface of which featured landmasses and [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]],<ref name="SWR" /> with its tropical regions having a [[Temperature/Legends|warm]] climate<ref name="Bane" /> and dry land being home to [[Plant/Legends|plants]].<ref name="Creatures" /> The planet's temperate and tropical waters were home to the [[Water/Legends|aquatic]] [[Mammal/Legends|mammal]] [[selligore]], which was a more-than-twenty-[[Meter/Legends|meters]]-long creature that [[Diet/Legends|fed]] on small [[Fish/Legends|fish]], [[Plankton/Legends|plankton]], and [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygenating]] plants. Selligores had long lived along the coasts of Corsin. They could survive in deep waters and briefly also on land but primarily inhabited shallow waters at depths of less than one hundred meters. Although selligore herds normally remained within their territory, some of them occasionally undertook once-in-a-generation migrations, usually due to their feeding grounds being infringed on. Generally, selligores avoided Corsin's traditional population; however, an exception was the creatures' relationship with the inhabitants of the [[Tinn'lyi Islands]].<ref name="Creatures" />

==History==
===Perils of Corsin===
{{Quote|Spacers' tales told of massive Mandalorian war fleets lurking in the dark beyond the Rim, but for a decade the Republic did little but watch and wait, even as Neo-Crusader raids imperiled worlds from Corsin to Azure.|Vilnau Tept, 412th Proceedings of Galactic Anthropology and History|<ref name="EGTW" />}}
[[File:Tskull_banner.svg|thumb|right|200px|The Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders (banner pictured) raided Corsin during the Mandalorian Wars.]]
Between approximately [[30,000 BBY]] and [[25,200 BBY]], Corsin was under the control of the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] of the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions']] [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. [[Realspace/Legends|Space]] surrounding the planet was explored by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] between [[8000 BBY]] and [[5500 BBY/Legends|5500 BBY]], and by approximately 5000 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]], Corsin was considered a part of the "civilized," or well-explored, portion of the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="TEA" /> As was later noted by [[Vilnau Teupt]] in the keynote address "[[Industry, Honor, Savagery: Shaping the Mandalorian Soul]]" at [[Brentaal Academy]]'s [[Proceedings of Galactic Anthropology and History|412th Proceedings of Galactic Anthropology and History]] in [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]], Corsin was among the worlds beyond the Republic's borders that were [[Raid on Corsin|raided]] by the [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]] movement of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] warrior culture between [[3976 BBY]] and [[3960 BBY]] as part of the [[Mandalorian Wars]].<ref name="EGTW" />

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: The Old Republic}}
Around [[3643 BBY]],<ref name="3643 BBY">Per the reasoning [[Template:TOR_dates|here]], Act I of ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' takes place around [[3643 BBY]]. Since players of ''The Old Republic'' can assign their companions on the mission "Renegade Scientist" independently of the main class storyline at any point during the game, the mission must take place at some point around 3643 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]].</ref> a [[Ronda's shuttle|shuttle]] carrying the renowned [[Biologist/Legends|bioanalyst]] [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Ronda]] crash-landed on Corsin, [[Death/Legends|killing]] the [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]]. An individual affiliated with one of the sides in the ongoing [[Sith Wars/Legends|struggle]] between the Republic and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]] subsequently dispatched a companion to investigate the crash, with the latter individual retrieving from the wreckage of the [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] remarkable specimens from Ronda's latest research.<ref name="Renegade Scientist">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Bioanalysis|Renegade Scientist}}</ref>
{{EndGame}}

===A Republic world===
{{Quote|While Ominaz won't see action until the Stassia Classic, Arrogantus will look to claim the top seed next month on Corsin at the Plooriod 940.|[[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]] report|<ref name="HNN">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|54|sports/1352_1.html|Ominaz Keeps Top Ranking}}</ref>}}
[[File:DarthZannah-RuleOfTwo.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Darth Zannah (pictured) impersonated the Jedi Nalia Adollu of Corsin.]]
The [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Gender/Legends|female]]<ref name="Bane" /> [[Human/Legends|Human]]<ref name="Adollu species">In ''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]'', [[Nalia Adollu]] is impersonated by [[Darth Zannah/Legends|Darth Zannah]], who, as part of her disguise, simply changes her [[Hair/Legends|hair]] [[Color/Legends|color]] and who is a [[Human/Legends|Human]] per ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''.</ref> [[Nalia Adollu]] was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] in the tropical regions of Corsin<ref name="Bane" /> around [[1010 BBY]],<ref name="Adollu age">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]'' establishes that [[Darth Zannah/Legends|Darth Zannah]] is ten [[Standard year/Legends|years]] old at the time of the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan]], which took place in [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] according to ''[[The Essential Atlas]]''. ''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]'' in turn establishes that Adollu was of similar age to Zannah.</ref> eventually traveling off-world and becoming a member of the Republic's [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="Bane" /> Approximately [[990 BBY|twenty years]] later,<ref name="990 BBY">The portion of ''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]'' in which [[Darth Zannah/Legends|Darth Zannah]] infiltrates the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] is set ten [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan]], which took place in [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] according to ''[[The Essential Atlas]]''.</ref> when the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Zannah/Legends|Darth Zannah]] infiltrated the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], she memorized Adollu's origin on Corsin as part of the process of impersonating her.<ref name="Bane" /> Corsin had become a part of Republic space by [[1004 BBY]], and at some point between that year and [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], during the [[Light and Darkness War|final phase]] of the [[Millennium/Legends|millennium]]-long [[New Sith Wars]], the Jedi Order emerged victorious over the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] in a [[Battle of Corsin|confrontation]] at Corsin.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:CorsinRetreat-EGTW.jpg|thumb|300px|Officers of the Galactic Republic's Planetary Security Forces met at Corsin Retreat.]]
After the operation known as the [[Mandalorian Excision]] of [[738 BBY]], [[Marshal/Legends|marshals]] and [[Admiral/Legends|admirals]] of the [[Planetary Security Forces]] of the Republic's member worlds met on Corsin, at an establishment known as the [[Corsin Retreat]], in order to discuss best practices for coordinating action among the security forces.<ref name="EGTW" /> [[Standard century/Legends|Centuries]] later, on the [[Great ReSynchronization|date]] [[22 BBY/Legends|13:5:2]], an issue of the [[HoloNet News CoCo District Edition|CoCo District Edition]] of the [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]] noted the upcoming [[Plooriod 940]] [[Swoop racing/Legends|swoop race]] that was set to take place on Corsin in the following [[Standard month/Legends|month]].<ref name="HNN" /> During the first campaigns of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in 22 BBY, the [[Third Mid Rim Army|Third Army]] of the Republic was tasked with engaging the [[Confederacy military/Legends|military forces]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] in Corsin's vicinity, and [[17 BBY/Legends|three years]] later, the planet fell within the borders of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="EGTW" />

===Regime change===
{{Quote|While Corsin's prior government established large habitats for the animals, the current Imperial regime has chosen not to prosecute violations of the statutes and is authorizing development of some habitat areas.|Holobrochure for the Tagge Holographic Museum of Chandrila|<ref name="Creatures" />}}
[[File:VorenNaal.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Voren Na'al experienced the Galactic Empire's crackdown on Corsin.]]
During the early stages of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Corsin hosted an annual [[Swoop/Legends|swoop]] race that was one of the most popular such events in the Greater Plooriod Cluster. At one point during that time, the Human [[Galactic News Service]]
[[Journalist/Legends|reporter]] [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]] was covering the race on Corsin. Excited at his assignment, he was watching the opening match of the race among other reporters in a press area. At that time,<ref name="GG1" /> as part of a brutal<ref name="Creatures" /> Imperial [[Crackdown on Corsin|subjugation]] of the planet,<ref name="SWR" /> a [[Platoon/Legends|platoon]] of Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] entered the press area and promptly arrested all the reporters with no explanation provided.<ref name="GG1">''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]''</ref>

Over the following three [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]], while Na'al and the other journalists were in detention,<ref name="GG1" /> the Empire forcibly deposed<ref name="GG1-2">[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope'', Second Edition]]</ref> Corsin's entire [[Corsin planetary government|planetary government]], replaced it with a pro-Imperial regime,<ref name="GG1" /> and instituted a military occupation.<ref name="SWR" /> Civil rights of the planet's population were rescinded, and it was submitted to the presence of military [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|police]].<ref name="GG1-2" /> After Na'al's release from detention—which was never justified to him—he was disturbed by the Imperial crackdown and its silencing of journalists; and as a result he eventually joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]].<ref name="GG1" /> Corsin eventually gained a measure of notoriety for its Imperial subjugation.<ref name="Creatures" />

Although the previous government of Corsin had designated extensive territories as habitats for the planet's selligore creatures, the pro-Imperial regime did not prosecute violations of the statutes concerning those habitats, and furthermore, it sanctioned the development of some of those areas. As a result, the selligores had access to shrinking territories where they could roam and feed, leading to a number of attacks on Humans and members of other [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] species. Several scientist attempted to persuaded Corsin's ruling regime to protect the selligores, using the special relationship between the creatures and the [[Tinn'lyi]] nation of the planet's Tinn'lyi Islands as an example of the benefits of such a course of action. Corsin was eventually mentioned in an entry of a [[Holo-brochure|holobrochure]] for the [[Tagge Holographic Museum]] of<ref name="Creatures" /> the Core Worlds planet<ref name="CSWE Chandrila">{{CSWECite|I|119|Chandrila}}</ref> [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]] dedicated to the selligore.<ref name="Creatures" />

===After the Empire===
[[File:ZsinjsEmpire7-8ABY-TEA.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Corsin was a part of Zsinj's Empire.]]
During the beginning of the Empire's fragmentation in the aftermath of the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] of [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Corsin became a part of the [[Zsinj's Empire|holdings]] of the Imperial [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Zsinj]]. In the [[5 ABY/Legends|following year]], the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] suffered a [[Battle of Corsin (5 ABY)|defeat]] to Zsinj's forces at Corsin, and the world remained under the warlord's control until [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]]. Corsin was located within the core territory of the [[Thrawn's confederation|confederation]] of Imperial forces [[Thrawn campaign|led]] by [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]], and it still lay within [[Imperial Space]] between [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]] and [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]].<ref name="TEA" />

Between [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]] and [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]], Corsin was situated within the territory of the New Republic.<ref name="EGTW" /> At some point between [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]] and [[26 ABY/Legends|26 ABY]], the Corsin system was [[Battle of the Corsin system|conquered]] by the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|extragalactic]] [[Yuuzhan Vong]] species as part of its [[Yuuzhan Vong War|invasion]] of the galaxy. It remained under the invaders' control until at least [[27 ABY/Legends|27 ABY]]. By [[137 ABY]], Corsin was part of the [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]] ruled by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Krayt]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|The Tinn'lyis will gather rich plant life and leave it on shore, while certain members of the Tinn'lyi nation will assist the selligores as they drag large nets behind them, scooping up large quantities of fish.|Holobrochure for the Tagge Holographic Museum of Chandrila|<ref name="Creatures" />}}
[[File:KethPlaying-FC.png|thumb|left|300px|Corsin claimed to be the birthplace of the hintaro game (pictured).]]
Corsin's Tinn'lyi Islands were home to the nation known as the Tinn'lyi. They maintained a symbiotic relationship with the planet's selligore animals. It involved the Tinn'lyi leaving ashore abundant amounts of plants for the creatures. In return, the selligores, assisted by the Tinn'lyi dragged large nets behind them, in the process collecting large quantities of fish for the native people to eat. The relationship had been the focus of extensive research by biologists.<ref name="Creatures" />

By the time of the Galactic Civil War, Corsin had long been considered a liberal and free-thinking world<ref name="GG1" /> and was known for its populace's love of life.<ref name="GG1-2" /> Before the Galactic Empire's crackdown on the world, the advocacy for freedom and peace from some of the members of its planetary government was comparable to that of<ref name="GG1" /> the Core Worlds<ref name="TEA" /> planet [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="GG1" />

Although both Corsin and [[Chazwa/Legends|Chazwa]],<ref name="Fly">''[[Fly Casual]]''</ref> an Inner Rim<ref name="EAOC Chazwa Corsin">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} — Based on corresponding data for [[Chazwa system/Legends|Chazwa system]] and [[Corsin system/Legends|Corsin system]]</ref> planet, claimed they were the birthplace of the [[Chance cube/Legends|dice]] game [[Hintaro/Legends|hintaro]], the game eventually became popular on many worlds, and it was more likely that the game evolved out of several similar games with different points of origin.<ref name="Fly" /> Around 25 ABY, the population of the Corsin [[Star system/Legends|system]] numbered between one hundred and five hundred million.<ref name="TEA" />

==Locations==
{{Quote|Selligores have largely remained apart from Corsin's traditional population. One exception to this are the natives of the Tinn'lyi Islands, who have long maintained a supportive relationship with these animals.|Holobrochure for the Tagge Holographic Museum of Chandrila|<ref name="Creatures" />}}
Corsin was the site of the Tinn'lyi Islands.<ref name="Creatures" /> The establishment known as the Corsin Retreat was also located on the planet. It was situated near a body of water and featured decorative plants, with lanes of aerial vehicles traversing above the retreat.<ref name="EGTW" />

==Behind the scenes==
Corsin was first mentioned in the [[1989]] sourcebook ''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]'', which was written by [[Grant S. Boucher]] and published by [[West End Games]] for use with ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="GG1" /> The planet was visually depicted for the first time in an illustration by [[Peter Venters]] included in the [[1994]] ''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'' sourcebook ''[[Creatures of the Galaxy]]''.<ref name="Creatures" /> The planet's first full appearance came in the [[1998]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']], which depicted it via an image also used to illustrate thirteen other worlds in the game.<ref name="SWR" /> Corsin was mentioned in a Bionanalysis Crew Skill mission of ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', a [[2011]] video game developed by [[BioWare]], though the information regarding the mission's outcome was later removed from the game.<ref name="Renegade Scientist" />

[[File:Tolonda-Voyages13.png|thumb|right|250px|''Voyages SF'' 13 placed Corsin in the Tolonda sector.]]
"[[Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are]]," a [[1990]] [[roleplaying game]] source article published in [[Voyages SF 13|''Voyages SF'' 13]], placed the Corsin system, and therefore Corsin itself, in the [[Tolonda sector/Legends|Tolonda sector]]. Since the article was released outside of the [[Lucas Licensing]] process, its [[canon]]icity within the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity was never confirmed.<ref name="Twinkle">{{VoyagesCite|13|Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are}}</ref> ''Star Wars: Rebellion'' later placed Corsin in the "Sesswenna sector,"<ref name="SWR" /> a misspelling of the [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]]. The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed Corsin in grid square M-7,<ref name="TEA" /> and the [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]] to the book eventually overrode both the ''Voyages SF'' 13 and ''Star Wars: Rebellion'' placements by instead establishing that the system was situated in the Greater Plooriod [[Sector/Legends|sector]].<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref>

Corsin was mentioned in [[Jedi Academy: Return of the Padawan|''Return of the Padawan'']], [[Jeffrey Brown]]'s [[2014]] second installment in the ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Academy]]'' series of non-canonical young-reader books. In the book, the Human [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Roan Novachez]] of the [[Coruscant Jedi Academy]], while preparing to visit his classmate [[Pasha]]'s [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Obroa-skai/Legends|Obroa-skai]] during [[Spring/Legends|spring]] break<ref name="Return">''[[Jedi Academy: Return of the Padawan]]''</ref> around [[195 BBY]],<ref name="ReturnDate">{{JediAcademyDates|2}}</ref> notes directions for traveling there on a sheet of [[Paper/Legends|paper]]. The notes instruct to travel "a bunch of [[Parsec/Legends|parsecs]]" along the Hydian Way away from the Core Worlds until Corsin is reached, at which point one must "turn right," transferring to a route<ref name="Return" />—the Vaathkree Trade Corridor<ref name="TEA" />—leading to Obroa-skai.<ref name="Return" />
